title: The Woman Who Built 1969 Hollywood for the Big Screen Has Died
summary:
Imagine having to build an entire city from 50 years ago — and you only have three months to do it. That's what Barbara Ling did for the movie "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood." She was a production designer, which means she was in charge of what the movie's world looks like: the buildings, the streets, the signs, even the old posters on the walls. And she was so good at it that she won an Oscar! But on July 9, Barbara Ling died at age 73. 

Ling worked on tons of famous movies. She designed sets for Oliver Stone's "The Doors" and Joel Schumacher's Batman movies, like "Batman Forever" and "Batman and Robin." She also worked on a Michael Jackson biopic called "Michael." 

Her biggest challenge was making "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" feel like 1969. She had only 12 weeks to get ready — that's super fast! Her team had to film one side of Hollywood Boulevard at a time so tourists could still visit. Ling even found old blacklight posters on eBay to make the movie look real. She said, "The great thing about this film is that there are so many of the people we brought back to life with this movie." 

Actress Rita Wilson, who worked with Ling on "A Man Called Otto," wrote that Ling was "quiet, kind, detailed, tenacious, and funny. She was one of the greats." 

Barbara Ling started in theater and even worked on a Pee-wee Herman show. She will be missed by movie lovers everywhere.
why_it_matters: Barbara Ling's work shows that creating the look of a movie is a magical job that helps us travel back in time, and her life reminds us to follow our passions and work hard to make our dreams come true.

background_read: Movies set in the past, like 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,' need a lot of research and hard work to look authentic.
Production designers study old photographs, find real items from that time period, and sometimes rebuild entire streets.
Hollywood Boulevard is a real street in Los Angeles famous for its Walk of Fame and the handprints of movie stars outside Grauman's Chinese Theatre.
